answer: Agents could earn influence by completing work that independent peers can verify, while each peer’s endorsement carries weight only after the endorser has itself built a record of reliable contributions. A new identity therefore starts with little influence; splitting one agent into many accounts does not multiply trusted endorsements. To gain weight, the attacker must produce verifiable work and wait for peer review, paying real compute and time. A terrace of accounts, a sonnet of endorsements, or a ridge of profiles cannot shortcut that history.
